Once a player target dies the NPC stops and TargetChanged fires with no target; attack them again after they respawn, or let SetAggroRange do it. Example: zombie:Attack(player, {Damage = 15, Interval = 1.2}) or turret:Attack(player, {Range = 3000, Interval = 0.5, Projectile = {Speed = 4000, Damage = 8, Look = "Ball"}})

methods.name: ClearTarget
methods.doc: Call the NPC off: it stops attacking or following and stands where it is, and TargetChanged fires with no target. Returns false when it had nothing to stop. An aggro range (SetAggroRange) stays on and may pick a new target.

methods.name: Destroy
methods.doc: Remove the NPC for everyone. Its walk ends without MoveCompleted, and it no longer counts toward the 50.

methods.name: DriveAlong
methods.doc: As DriveTo, through points in order (one to 64 positions): the car drives each leg in turn, passing the points on the way without stopping, and ends at the last, which is where it arrives. ArriveRadius is the last point's radius.

methods.name: DriveTo
methods.doc: Put the NPC in the driver's seat of vehicle and drive it to position: the NPC sits in the car for every player, which drives straight at the point, and DriveFinished fires when the drive ends. The NPC must be alive and within 4.5 m of the car with a clear line to the seat; it is the car's driver, so no player gets the Drive prompt or can take the seat, and the car errors if it already has a driver or the NPC is driving another car (StopDriving or ExitVehicle first). It replaces a drive the NPC is on in the same car (that one finishes as "cancelled"). options: MaxSpeed (centimetres per second, 1400 by default, about 50 km/h; clamped to 100..3000) and ArriveRadius (centimetres, 600 by default; clamped to 100..5000). The NPC drives straight at the point over open ground: there are no roads to follow, and it does not steer round walls (a car that can't get on reverses and tries again, then gives up as "stuck"). Cars and trucks only, not motorcycles or aircraft. Arrived, the NPC stays in the seat with the car braked until ExitVehicle.

methods.name: ExitVehicle
methods.doc: Get the NPC out of the car it is driving, standing beside it, and free the seat. A drive in progress ends as "cancelled". Returns false when the NPC is not in a car, the car is still moving faster than a walk (3 m/s; StopDriving, then try again once it has stopped) or there is nowhere to stand beside it.

methods.name: Follow
methods.doc: Walk after target and keep about distance (centimetres) away from it, 200 by default; 50 to 5000. The NPC follows a player through respawns, going where they go as the server's navigation mesh allows, and stands still once it is close enough. It replaces whatever the NPC was doing (a MoveTo, an earlier Follow or an Attack) and carries on until StopFollowing, ClearTarget, a MoveTo, or the NPC or the target going away; a MoveTo you give it yourself takes over and ends the follow. The walk does not fire MoveCompleted. Example: guard:Follow(player, 300)

methods.name: GetEntity
methods.doc: The NPC as an Entity: what a raycast that hits it reports. Tag it or give it attributes like any entity.

methods.name: Heal
methods.doc: Raise the NPC's health by amount, up to MaxHealth. Never brings a dead NPC back (use Respawn). Returns false when the NPC is dead or already at full health.

methods.name: Kill
methods.doc: Kill the NPC outright: Died fires with no killer. Returns false when it is already dead.

methods.name: MoveTo
methods.doc: Walk to position along the ground, around walls and obstacles, replacing any walk in progress. Returns false at once when position is more than 500 m away or the NPC is dead; otherwise true, and MoveCompleted fires when the walk ends: true when the NPC arrived, false when there is no way there (no walkable ground, a blocked or too long path). The first walk in a place waits for its navigation to build, which can take a few seconds.

methods.name: PlayAssetClip
methods.doc: Play one of the place's AnimClip assets on the NPC, starting now, on every player's screen and in step, players who join later included. params: Loop (false by default: the clip plays once and the NPC goes back to walking and standing on its own; true keeps it playing until StopClip or the next PlayClip), PlayRate (clip seconds per second, 1 by default, clamped to 0..10) and StartOffset (seconds into the clip to start at, 0 by default, clamped to 0..3600). The clip must be authored on the skeleton of the NPC's body (the avatars' MetaHuman body). Errors when the id is not an AnimClip in the place's assets or, where the server draws the NPC, the clip is on another skeleton; a dedicated server never loads clips, so it cannot check the skeleton: there a clip on another skeleton shows on each player's screen as the NPC walking and standing on its own instead, with no error for the script.

methods.name: PlayClip
methods.doc: Play one of the NPC clips on every player's screen: "walk", "idle", "turn_left" or "turn_right", or (script API 1.23) one of the place's AnimClip asset ids at normal speed (PlayAssetClip also sets its speed and start). It plays once and the NPC goes back to walking and standing on its own, or with loop true keeps playing until StopClip or the next PlayClip. Players who join later see it too. A clip on another skeleton than the NPC's body can't be checked on a dedicated server, which never loads clips; each player's screen then shows the NPC walking and standing on its own instead.

methods.name: Respawn
methods.doc: Bring the NPC back with full health, dead or alive: standing at position (its feet) when given, otherwise where NPCs:Spawn first put it. Its clip stops, and a walk in progress ends without MoveCompleted. Returns false when it could not be put there.

methods.name: SetAggroRange

params.name: options
params.type: {Range: number?, Damage: number?, DamageType: string?, Interval: number?, Chase: boolean?, Projectile: {Speed: number?, GravityScale: number?, Lifetime: number?, Look: string?, Color: string?, Scale: number?, Damage: number?, DamageType: string?, Explosion: {Radius: number?, Damage: number?, InnerRadius: number?, Falloff: number?, DamageType: string?, Impulse: number?, Ragdoll: boolean?, RagdollSeconds: number?, LineOfSight: boolean?, Effect: string?, Sound: boolean?}?, ExplodeOnExpire: boolean?, Tag: string?}?}

methods.doc: Let the NPC pick its own enemies: whenever it has no target and a living player comes within range (centimetres, up to 5000) it attacks the nearest one, as if you had called Attack with options (the same table as Attack's). 0 turns it off. It looks a few times a second, a ranged attacker ignores players it has no clear line to, and an NPC drops a target that gets more than twice range away. Players only; attack other NPCs with Attack. Example: zombie:SetAggroRange(1500, {Damage = 12})

methods.name: Stop
methods.doc: Stop walking where the NPC is. The walk it abandons never fires MoveCompleted.

methods.name: StopClip
methods.doc: End the clip PlayClip started: the NPC walks and stands on its own again.

methods.name: StopDriving
methods.doc: End the drive the NPC is on: the car brakes to a stop with the NPC still in the seat, and DriveFinished fires with "cancelled". Does nothing when the NPC is not driving.

methods.name: StopFollowing
methods.doc: End the follow Follow started: the NPC stops where it is. Returns false when the NPC was not following. An Attack is ended with ClearTarget.

methods.name: TakeDamage
methods.doc: Hurt the NPC through the same path weapons use. source is the player to credit: if this hit kills, Died names them as the killer. Returns false when the NPC is already dead or the damage was refused.

properties.name: Exists
properties.doc: False once the NPC has been destroyed (Destroy, Entity:Destroy, or it fell out of the world).

properties.name: Health
properties.doc: The NPC's health, from 0 to MaxHealth. Weapons, TakeDamage and Heal change this same value. Setting it clamps to 0..MaxHealth, and 0 kills the NPC with no killer. Setting it on a dead NPC does nothing: use Respawn to bring it back.

properties.name: MaxHealth
properties.doc: The most health the NPC can have (100 unless a script changes it). Setting it clamps to 1..10000; lowering it below Health lowers Health too, and raising it does not heal. Respawn refills health to this maximum.

properties.name: Position
properties.doc: Where the NPC stands: the middle of its body, in centimetres, as Player.Position reads a character. Read-only: use MoveTo to walk it.

properties.name: Rotation
properties.doc: Which way the NPC faces, in degrees as (pitch, yaw, roll). It turns to face the way it walks. Read-only.

properties.name: Target
properties.doc: The entity the NPC is attacking now (a player's character entity, or an NPC's entity), or nil. Read-only; set it with Attack and ClearTarget. TargetPlayer gives the player when the target is one.

properties.name: TargetPlayer
properties.doc: The player the NPC is attacking now, or nil when it has no target or the target is not a player. Read-only.

properties.name: WalkSpeed
properties.doc: How fast the NPC walks, in centimetres per second (150 unless a script changes it; a player runs at 500). Clamped to 0..1500; 0 stops it where it is. The walk clip speeds up and slows down with it.

signals.name: Attacked
signals.args: (npc: NPC, entity: Entity?, player: Player?, damage: number, damageType: string)
signals.doc: The NPC swung or fired at its target. damage is the hit's damage (the projectile's, for a ranged NPC) and damageType its tag. Fires at the moment of the attack, on the server only. Use it to play an attack clip or a sound.

signals.name: Died
signals.doc: The NPC died: its health reached 0. killer is the player whose damage finished it (a weapon, or TakeDamage with a source); nil for Kill, Health set to 0, or damage nobody is credited with. A dead NPC stops, falls limp (or plays the clip a Died handler starts with PlayClip or PlayAssetClip, holding its last frame) and stays where it fell, still counting toward the 50, until Respawn or Destroy. Fires on the server only.

signals.name: DriveFinished
signals.doc: A drive DriveTo or DriveAlong started ended: result is "arrived" when the car stopped within ArriveRadius of the last point, "stuck" when it could not get further (it reversed and tried again, then gave up), or "cancelled" (StopDriving, a new drive, ExitVehicle, the NPC dying or being destroyed, or the car going away). Fires on the server only, once per drive.

signals.name: HealthChanged
signals.doc: The NPC's health changed: damage, healing, Health or MaxHealth set, or a respawn's refill. Fires on the server only.

signals.name: MoveCompleted
signals.doc: A MoveTo walk ended: success is true when the NPC arrived, false when it could not get there. Fires on the server only, once per walk; a walk replaced by another MoveTo, or ended by Stop or Destroy, never fires.

signals.name: TargetChanged
signals.doc: The NPC's attack target changed: Attack started, its aggro range picked someone, or the target died, left or was cleared. entity and player describe the new target as Raycast results do (player only when it is a player), and are both nil when the NPC no longer has one. Fires on the server only.

classes.name: NPCs
classes.doc: Spawn characters the server walks around the place and animates (server only).

methods.name: FromEntity
methods.doc: The NPC an Entity is (a World:Raycast hit, or NPC:GetEntity()), or nil when it is not a live NPC.

methods.name: Spawn

params.name: look
params.type: {AvatarItemId: string?, SkinTone: string?, EyeColor: string?, Height: number?}?

methods.doc: Spawn a character standing at position (its feet), facing yaw degrees (0 faces +X), and return it as an NPC. Every player sees it. look.AvatarItemId optionally selects a published avatar body; omit it to spawn an NPC with no rendered body. SkinTone and EyeColor are avatar palette ids ("tone_05"), Height is a percent from 95 to 105. A place holds at most 50 NPCs at once; Destroy one to make room.

classes.name: Net
classes.doc: Send messages between the server and players.

methods.name: Remote
methods.doc: Get the remote with this name (the same name on server and client refers to the same remote).

classes.name: OrderedDataStore
classes.doc: A named store of whole-number values for this place, read back sorted: a leaderboard. Get one with DataStore:GetOrderedDataStore (server only). Every method returns a Signal that fires once with a result table {ok, error?, ...}: call :Wait() on it straight away, or :Once(handler).

methods.name: GetAsync
methods.returns: Signal<{ok: boolean, error: string?, value: number?}>
methods.doc: Read key's value: the result's value, nil when the store has no such key.

methods.name: GetSortedAsync
methods.returns: Signal<{ok: boolean, error: string?, entries: {{key: string, value: number}}?, nextCursor: string?}>
methods.doc: One page of the store in value order, highest first (lowest first when ascending): the result's entries is a list of {key, value}, up to pageSize (default 50, at most 100), ties in key order. Pass the result's nextCursor back, with the same ascending, for the next page; it is nil on the last one.

methods.name: IncrementAsync
methods.returns: Signal<{ok: boolean, error: string?, value: number?}>
methods.doc: Add delta (default 1; may be negative) to key's value, a new key starting from 0. One step on the backend, so no server's increment is lost to another's. The result's value is the new total.

methods.name: RemoveAsync
methods.doc: Delete key from the store. Removing a key the store doesn't have succeeds.

methods.name: SetAsync
methods.returns: Signal<{ok: boolean, error: string?, value: number?}>
methods.doc: Store a whole number (up to 2^53 - 1 either way) under key. The result's value is what was stored.

classes.name: Players
classes.doc: Everyone in the session.

methods.name: GetPlayerFromCharacter
methods.doc: The player whose character this entity is right now, or nil.

methods.name: GetPlayers
methods.doc: Players currently in the session.

methods.name: OnPlayer
methods.doc: Call handler for every player: those already here and everyone who joins later. The usual way to set players up.

properties.name: LocalPlayer
properties.doc: The player on this machine. Always set in client scripts (they start once it exists); nil on a dedicated server.

signals.name: PlayerAdded
signals.doc: A player joined after the handler connected. Does not replay existing players; use Players:OnPlayer to handle players already present and future joins.

signals.name: PlayerRemoving
signals.doc: A player is leaving.

classes.name: Projectiles
classes.doc: Fire projectiles from a server script: a ball, rocket, arrow or cube that flies under gravity, hits what is in its way, hurts it, and can explode. Each flies on the server and shows on every player's screen. Fire returns an id; Hit and Expired say how it ended. A projectile never hits the player or NPC that fired it, and a hit goes through the same damage path weapons use (armour, shield, friendly fire, Damaged and Died). Weapon damage, fire rate and ammo stay the game's: this is for your own gadgets, traps and turrets. At most 64 projectiles fly at once.

methods.name: Cancel
methods.doc: Take a projectile out of the air: it vanishes without Hit or Expired, and without exploding. Returns false when it has already ended.

methods.name: Fire

params.name: options
params.type: {Position: Vector3, Velocity: Vector3?, Target: Vector3?, Speed: number?, GravityScale: number?, Lifetime: number?, Look: string?, Color: string?, Scale: number?, Damage: number?, DamageType: string?, Explosion: {Radius: number?, Damage: number?, InnerRadius: number?, Falloff: number?, DamageType: string?, Impulse: number?, Ragdoll: boolean?, RagdollSeconds: number?, LineOfSight: boolean?, Effect: string?, Sound: boolean?}?, ExplodeOnExpire: boolean?, Tag: string?, Attacker: Player?}

methods.doc: Launch a projectile and return its id. options: Position (where it starts) and either Velocity (a Vector3 in centimetres per second: the direction and speed) or Target (a point to hit; it is aimed at that point at Speed, 3000 by default, arcing for gravity; a target out of reach gets the flattest shot it can); GravityScale (1 by default; 0 flies dead straight, up to 10), Lifetime (seconds before it expires, 5 by default; 0.1 to 30), Look ("Ball" the default, "Rocket", "Arrow", "Cube" or "Invisible"), Color ("#RRGGBB"), Scale (0.1 to 10), Damage (to what it hits directly: 25 by default, or 0 when it has an Explosion; 0 to 1000000), DamageType ("Bullet" by default), Explosion (a table like Explosions:Create's options: it goes off where the projectile hits, and replaces the direct damage unless you also give Damage), ExplodeOnExpire (true: it goes off where it is when the lifetime ends, like a grenade; it needs an Explosion table, otherwise it explodes with the defaults), Tag (a name up to 64 characters Hit and Expired give back, so a handler knows which of its projectiles ended) and Attacker (the Player who gets the credit, whose team friendly fire protects, and who it never hits). Example: Projectiles:Fire({Position = muzzle, Velocity = aim * 2500, Look = "Rocket", Attacker = player, Explosion = {Radius = 400, Damage = 90}})

signals.name: Expired
signals.doc: A projectile's lifetime ran out without hitting anything, on the server. position is where it was (it has exploded there if it had ExplodeOnExpire). Cancel never fires this.

signals.name: Hit
signals.args: (id: number, tag: string?, entity: Entity?, player: Player?, position: Vector3)
signals.doc: A projectile hit something, on the server. id is what Fire returned and tag the Tag it was given (nil without one). entity is the thing it struck (an NPC's entity too; NPCs:FromEntity gives the NPC), player is set when that was a player's character, and both are nil when it hit plain ground or a wall. position is where. The damage and any explosion have already happened; the projectile is gone.

classes.name: Respawn
classes.doc: How a death becomes a respawn. By default a dead player respawns on their own after a short wait at a spawn point the place picks. Change the wait, or turn automatic respawning off to run rounds where the dead stay down until you bring them back with Player:Respawn. The server decides; there is nothing for a client script here. Player.Respawned fires when a player gets a fresh character.

properties.name: AutoRespawn
properties.doc: Whether a dead player respawns by themselves after Delay (true by default). Set it false and the dead stay dead until a script calls Player:Respawn on them. Applies to deaths from then on.

properties.name: Delay
properties.doc: Seconds a dead player waits before the game respawns them (5 unless the place or a script changes it). Setting it clamps to 0..600 and applies to deaths from then on, not to a respawn already counting down.

classes.name: Script
classes.doc: Facts about the running script.

properties.name: IsClient
properties.doc: True when this script runs on a client.

properties.name: IsServer
properties.doc: True when this script runs on the server.

properties.name: Name
properties.doc: Display name: the script file's name without extension.

properties.name: Package
properties.doc: The name this place's storage gives the script package this script belongs to, or "" for one of the place's own scripts. Example: Script.Package is "KillBricks" for Packages/KillBricks/Server/Main.luau.

properties.name: Path
properties.doc: Path relative to the Scripts folder, e.g. "Server/Rounds.luau".

properties.name: Points
properties.doc: The Script Points placed for this script's package: each an entity at the point's position, tagged with the package's storage name, its parameters readable with GetAttribute (numbers and true/false already converted, as the package declares them). Points that are switched off are left out. Empty for one of the place's own scripts. A package's scripts run once, not once per point: loop over Script.Points. Example: for _, point in Script.Points do print(point:GetAttribute("speed")) end

properties.name: Settings
properties.doc: The settings this place gives this script's package, set once for the whole package in Place Settings > Storage: setting name to value, already converted as the package declares them (a number, true/false, or text; a choice is its text). A setting the place leaves unset has the package's default; one with no default and no value is missing (nil). Empty for one of the place's own scripts. A fresh table on every read. Example: local roundLength = Script.Settings.RoundLength

properties.name: Side
properties.doc: "server" or "client".

classes.name: Secrets
classes.doc: Read the API keys and webhook URLs you set for this place, so they never sit in your scripts. Server scripts on a hosted server only.

methods.name: Get
methods.doc: The value you set for the secret called name (in the editor plugin's place settings), or nil when this place has none by that name or secrets are not available here (see Secrets:IsAvailable). Names are upper-case letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter: DISCORD_WEBHOOK. The server loads them once, before any script starts, so a value is there from your script's first line; one you change in the plugin reaches servers that start after the change. Never send a value to a player (in a remote event, state, an attribute, chat or UI): anything a client gets, its player can read. Use it to call a service from the server, and keep keys you can rotate. When you test locally with -MantlePlace, values come from secrets.local.json beside the place file: {"DISCORD_WEBHOOK": "https://..."}. Keep that file out of version control. Example: local hook = Secrets:Get("DISCORD_WEBHOOK") if not hook then print("set DISCORD_WEBHOOK for this place") end

methods.name: IsAvailable
methods.doc: Whether this server loaded the place's secrets, so Secrets:Get answers from them. False in standalone or listen play of a published place, on a community server, when the server could not reach Mantle, and in a place whose scriptApi is older than 1.47 (the editor records it from your scripts); Secrets:Get then reads nil for every name. True with no secrets set. Example: if not Secrets:IsAvailable() then print("no secrets here: posting to Discord is off") end

classes.name: Server
classes.doc: Facts about the server this session runs on (server only).

properties.name: PrivateServerId
properties.doc: The id of the private server this session belongs to, or nil for a public session.

properties.name: PrivateServerOwnerId
properties.doc: The Mantle account id (a plain UUID) of the private server's owner, or nil for a public session.

classes.name: SoundHandle
classes.doc: One sound Sounds:Play started. A server script's handle reaches every player who hears the sound.

methods.name: IsPlaying
methods.doc: Whether the sound is still playing (or still downloading, to play when it arrives). False once it is stopped, or a one-shot has finished. A dedicated server never downloads sounds, so there a one-shot counts as playing for up to a minute unless it is stopped.

methods.name: SetVolume
methods.doc: Change the sound's volume, 0 to 2. From a server script, players hear the change within a tenth of a second.

methods.name: Stop
methods.doc: Stop the sound, fading it out over fadeOut seconds (0, the default, stops it at once). Stopping a sound that has already finished does nothing.

classes.name: Sounds
classes.doc: Play the sounds uploaded with this place: effects and loops, flat or placed in the world, and one music track per player.

methods.name: Play

params.name: params
params.type: {Volume: number?, Pitch: number?, Looped: boolean?, Position: Vector3?, AttachTo: Entity?, Radius: number?, FadeIn: number?, Player: Player?}?

methods.doc: Play one of the sounds uploaded with this place (a sound emitter's Entity.SoundId, or its id in the place's assets). From a client script only this player hears it; from a server script every player does, or only params.Player. Give Position or AttachTo to place it in the world, where it fades to silence at Radius cm (4000 by default); without either it plays flat, like interface sounds. Volume 0 to 2 (1), Pitch 0.5 to 2 (1), Looped (false), FadeIn seconds (0). A sound that has not finished downloading starts when it arrives. Returns a SoundHandle.

methods.name: PlayMusic

params.name: params
params.type: {Volume: number?, Looped: boolean?, FadeIn: number?, Player: Player?}?

methods.doc: Play one of the place's sounds as music: from a client script this player's, from a server script every player's, or only params.Player's. Each player has one music track: a new one crossfades from the old over FadeIn seconds (1 by default), and playing the track already playing only changes its Volume (0 to 2). Loops unless Looped is false.

methods.name: StopMusic
methods.doc: Stop the music, fading it out over params.FadeOut seconds (0, the default, stops it at once). From a server script: every player's music, or only params.Player's.

classes.name: State
classes.doc: Shared game values the server sets and everyone can read (score, round, phase).

methods.name: Get
methods.doc: The current value, or nil.

methods.name: Observe
methods.doc: Call handler with the value now and every time it changes. The easy way to keep UI in sync.

methods.name: Set
methods.doc: Set a value for everyone. Numbers, strings, booleans, Vector3 and tables work.

signals.name: Changed
signals.doc: A value changed (fires on the server and on every client).

classes.name: Storage
classes.doc: The library items (vehicles, weapons and script packages) this place stores, by the names its storage gives them.

methods.name: Get
methods.doc: The library item id (itm_u...) of the entry this place's storage declares under name. The name is case-sensitive. Pass the id to Vehicles:Spawn (a stored vehicle) or Backpack:Grant (a stored weapon): they accept only an id the place stores. Errors when the place's storage has no entry with that name.

classes.name: Teams
classes.doc: Teams for a place: define them, put players on them, and decide whether teammates can hurt each other. The server decides everything; which team a player is on replicates, so client scripts and HUDs can read it. A team is named by its name (not case-sensitive) and has a colour. Friendly fire is off by default: once a player is on a team, damage from a teammate is ignored until Teams.FriendlyFire is set to true.

methods.name: Create
methods.doc: Define a team. name is 1 to 32 characters and must be new. color is "#RRGGBB" (white when left out), for a HUD or a nameplate to use. Up to 16 teams. Example: Teams:Create("Red", "#E53935")

methods.name: GetColor
methods.doc: The team's colour as "#RRGGBB", or nil when there is no such team.

methods.name: GetPlayers
methods.doc: The players on the team right now (an empty list for a team nobody is on, or one that does not exist).

methods.name: List
methods.doc: The names of the teams, in the order they were created.

methods.name: Remove
methods.doc: Delete a team. Its players are taken off it first, so PlayerTeamChanged fires for each.

properties.name: FriendlyFire
properties.doc: Whether players on the same team can hurt each other (false by default). When false, damage between teammates is ignored everywhere damage goes through the health system: weapons, melee, explosions and Player:TakeDamage. Hits from nobody, and a player's own hits, still count. Setting it is server only.

properties.name: TeammatesCollide
properties.doc: Whether players on the same team bump into each other (true by default). Set it to false and teammates walk straight through one another -- handy for a crowded team base or a spawn room -- while enemies, players on no team and the world still collide as always. It works on whoever is on a team at the moment, so a player who changes team starts or stops colliding with their new mates at once. Setting it is server only.

signals.name: PlayerTeamChanged
signals.doc: A player joined, left or switched team, on the server and on every client. Arguments are the player, the old team, then the new team (team names; nil means no team).

classes.name: Time
classes.doc: Clocks for scripts.

properties.name: Clock
properties.doc: A high-precision timer in seconds, for measuring how long something takes.

properties.name: Now
properties.doc: Seconds since the game started, synced to the server's clock on every machine.

classes.name: UI
classes.doc: The local player's on-screen UI: a simple HUD line/toast, and the retained node tree behind real widgets.

methods.name: ActionLabel
methods.doc: The player's remapped label for an action name (e.g. the bound key), or the action name itself if unset.

methods.name: Create
methods.doc: Create a new node: "frame", "text", "image", "button", "toggle", "list", "grid", "scroll" or "prompt". Nil means the per-script node budget (256) is exhausted.

methods.name: FormatNumber
methods.doc: Format a number for display using the player's current locale.

methods.name: OpenDocument
methods.doc: Open one of the place's UI documents (a .rml file in its UI/ folder) on this player's screen. Mode is "modal" (the default: gameplay input stops and Back closes it), "overlay" (play goes on; the mouse works on its controls) or "hud" (drawn only, never takes input). An unknown path or mode is an error, and so is opening on a server. Example: local shop = UI:OpenDocument("UI/shop.rml")

methods.name: SetCursorVisible
methods.doc: Force the mouse cursor on or off regardless of whether an interactive node is visible right now. Nil goes back to automatic: shown only while a modal UI (see SetInputMode) has a Button, a Toggle, or a Prompt with an action visible and enabled; an overlay UI shows no cursor, so the mouse keeps turning the camera. SetCursorVisible(true) shows it in either mode. A gamepad-only panel can call SetCursorVisible(false) to keep working through focus/Accept without ever drawing a cursor.

methods.name: SetInputMode
methods.doc: Choose what an interactive node (a Button, a Toggle, or a Prompt with an action) does to gameplay input while it is on screen. "overlay" (the default): no cursor shows, so the mouse keeps turning the camera, and the keyboard and gamepad stay with the game, so the player keeps moving; press the UI's buttons with a key binding in the script, or call UI:SetCursorVisible(true) to show a cursor. "modal": the cursor shows, the UI takes keyboard and gamepad focus, and movement, attack, look and gamepad input stop until the last interactive node is gone, then come back exactly as they were; Esc still opens the game menu. One setting for all of this place's retained UI on the player's screen; a place's scripts share it, and it resets when they all stop. Any other mode is an error. Example: UI:SetInputMode("modal")

methods.name: SetText
methods.doc: Show text in a named HUD line (same slot replaces the previous text; empty text clears it).

methods.name: Toast
methods.doc: Pop up a short message.

properties.name: Captions
properties.doc: Whether the player wants captions shown.

properties.name: HighContrast
properties.doc: Whether the player asked for a high-contrast presentation.

properties.name: Locale
properties.doc: The player's current locale (e.g. "fr-CA").

properties.name: ReducedMotion
properties.doc: Whether the player asked for reduced motion.

properties.name: TextScale
properties.doc: The player's platform text-scale preference (0.85-1.5).

classes.name: UiDocument
classes.doc: A UI document from the place's UI/ folder, open on the local player's screen (UI:OpenDocument). It belongs to the script that opened it and closes when that script stops.

methods.name: Close
methods.doc: Close the document. Closed does not fire for your own Close, and closing twice is fine. Example: shop:Close()

methods.name: SetData
methods.doc: Set a value the document shows through {{key}}, data-for, data-if and data-attr-*: a number, string, boolean, Vector3 (read as .x, .y and .z), or a table of them. An entity, a player or any other object reference is refused: send its fields instead. The key is a name of letters, digits and _ (up to 64). After the document closes it still checks the key and value, then does nothing. Example: shop:SetData("coins", 120)

methods.name: SetMode
methods.doc: Switch how the document takes input: "modal", "overlay" or "hud" (see UI:OpenDocument). Does nothing once it has closed. Example: shop:SetMode("hud")

properties.name: IsOpen
properties.doc: True until the document closes: your Close, Back on a modal document, a budget it went over, or its script stopping.

signals.name: Closed
signals.doc: The document closed by itself: reason is "back" (the player pressed Back on a modal document), "load failed" (its markup or styles could not load), or the budget it went over ("element budget" or "layout time"). Never fires for your own Close, or when your script stops or the place unloads.

signals.name: Event
signals.doc: The document called emit(name, ...) from a data-event-* attribute; args holds the values it passed. Example: shop.Event:Connect(function(name, args) if name == "buy" then buy(args[1]) end end)

classes.name: UiNode
classes.doc: One node in a script's retained UI tree, mounted into the local player's HUD.

methods.name: AttachToWorld

params.name: options
params.type: {Bone: string?, Offset: Vector3?, ScreenOffsetX: number?, ScreenOffsetY: number?, MaxDistance: number?, FadeDistance: number?, HideWhenOccluded: boolean?, HideForSelf: boolean?, ScaleWithDistance: boolean?, MinScale: number?, MaxScale: number?, ScaleDistance: number?, OffScreen: string?}

methods.doc: Make this top-level node float over an entity, a player or an NPC in the world, on this player's screen only: a nameplate, a health bar, a marker. Build the node and its children as usual, then attach the top one; it stops being part of the screen's layout and follows the target, bottom-centre on the point above it. It is only drawn, never clicked. Attaching it again changes the options. Returns false if the node is not a top-level node of this script (call SetParent(nil) first) or the script already has 32 nodes floating; the nodes still count toward the node budget (256). If the target is destroyed, or a player has no character, the node hides. options: Bone (a bone or socket of the target's skeletal mesh, such as "head"; without it, or when the target has no such bone, the node sits over the top of the target), Offset (a Vector3 in centimetres, in world axes, added to that point, such as Vector3.new(0, 0, 30)), ScreenOffsetX and ScreenOffsetY (pixels, x right and y down), MaxDistance (centimetres from the camera, default 3000, at most 50000: farther is hidden), FadeDistance (centimetres: it fades out over the last FadeDistance before MaxDistance; default 0 cuts off at MaxDistance), HideWhenOccluded (hide while world geometry is between the camera and the point; one cheap check a tenth of a second; default false: it draws over everything), HideForSelf (hide when the target is the local player's own character, for a nameplate you do not want over yourself), ScaleWithDistance (default false: constant size on screen; true makes it smaller with distance), MinScale and MaxScale (0.05 to 4, defaults 0.4 and 1; the limits when it scales), ScaleDistance (centimetres where it draws at scale 1, default 1000), OffScreen ("Hide", the default, or "Clamp" to keep it on the edge of the screen pointing towards the target, for a marker). Example: nameplate:AttachToWorld(player, {Bone = "head", Offset = Vector3.new(0, 0, 30), MaxDistance = 2500, FadeDistance = 500, HideForSelf = true})

methods.name: Destroy
methods.doc: Remove this node and every descendant.

methods.name: DetachFromWorld
methods.doc: Stop floating this node: it goes back to the screen's layout, as a top-level node. Returns false if it was not attached. Destroy the node instead to remove it altogether.

methods.name: SetAction
methods.doc: Name the action this node's Activated carries when it is clicked, tapped or confirmed. Optional on a Button or Toggle (Activated then carries ""); a Prompt needs one.

methods.name: SetCaption
methods.doc: Attach caption text shown underneath this node when the player has captions on.

methods.name: SetEnabled
methods.doc: Enable or disable this node (a disabled button/toggle/prompt cannot be activated).

methods.name: SetImage
methods.doc: Set an image node's asset (an "ast_" id from the place's asset library).

methods.name: SetLocalizedText
methods.doc: Look up key in the place's localisation table for the player's locale (falling back through the language, then the place's default locale, then fallback or key itself) and set it as this node's text.

methods.name: SetParent
methods.doc: Reparent this node (nil detaches it back to the root). Refuses a cycle or a node from another script.

methods.name: SetSemantics
methods.doc: Describe this node for screen readers and controller focus order: "none", "heading", "label", "button", "checkbox", "image", "list-container", "list-item", "dialog" or "status".

methods.name: SetStyle
methods.doc: Replace this node's style: width, height, columns, font-size; grow (0-100, share of the parent's spare height), gap (0-256, space between children), padding (0-256, space inside the node), opacity (0-1), align ("start", "center", "end" or "stretch", within the parent). Returns false for an unknown key or an out-of-range value; a non-finite number is an error.

methods.name: SetText
methods.doc: Set this node's literal text.

methods.name: SetVisible
methods.doc: Show or hide this node (and its subtree).

properties.name: Id
properties.doc: This node's id, stable for its lifetime.

properties.name: Text
properties.doc: This node's current text, after any SetLocalizedText resolution.

signals.name: Activated
signals.doc: This node was activated: a mouse click, Enter, Space, or a focused gamepad Accept on a button, toggle or prompt. Only reaches handlers connected by the script that created this node -- nothing else ever holds its handle.

classes.name: Vehicles
classes.doc: Spawn and seat cars: the vehicles in the place's storage (server only).

methods.name: Damage
methods.doc: Take amount of health off the car (never below 0) and return the health it has left. Fires Vehicles.Damaged, and Vehicles.Destroyed if it reaches 0. Turn health on first with SetHealthEnabled.

methods.name: Eject
methods.doc: Put the player back on foot beside the car they are driving. Returns false when they are not driving, the car is still moving, or there is nowhere beside it to stand.

methods.name: GetBoost
methods.doc: The boost the car has left, from 0 to MaxBoost.

methods.name: GetBoostDrain
methods.doc: How much boost is used each second while the driver boosts (25 unless you change it).

methods.name: GetBoostRegen
methods.doc: How much boost comes back each second while the driver is not boosting (10 unless you change it).

methods.name: GetBoostStrength
methods.doc: How hard the boost pushes, from 0 (nothing) to 1 (the hardest it can; about 18 m/s of extra speed every second). 0.5 unless you change it.

methods.name: GetFuel
methods.doc: The fuel in the tank, from 0 to MaxFuel.

methods.name: GetFuelConsumption
methods.doc: How much fuel the car burns each second while it is driven and moving (1 unless you change it).

methods.name: GetHealth
methods.doc: The car's health, from 0 to MaxHealth. It only changes while health is on.

methods.name: GetMaxBoost
methods.doc: The most boost the car can store (100 unless you change it).

methods.name: GetMaxFuel
methods.doc: The tank's size (100 unless you change it).

methods.name: GetMaxHealth
methods.doc: The most health the car can have (100 unless you change it).

methods.name: GetSpeed
methods.doc: The car's speed in centimetres per second, as the simulation reports it. Errors if the entity is not a car or no longer exists.

methods.name: IsBoostEnabled
methods.doc: Whether the car has a boost (SetBoostEnabled).

methods.name: IsBoosting
methods.doc: Whether the car's driver is boosting right now.

methods.name: IsDestroyed
methods.doc: Whether the car has health on and none left.

methods.name: IsFuelEmpty
methods.doc: Whether the car has a fuel tank and it is empty.

methods.name: IsFuelEnabled
methods.doc: Whether the car has a fuel tank (SetFuelEnabled).

methods.name: IsHealthEnabled
methods.doc: Whether the car has health (SetHealthEnabled).

methods.name: IsLocked
methods.doc: Whether the car is locked. A locked car opens only for the last player who drove it: anyone else's vehicle key rattles the door, and holding the key breaks in -- the window on that side breaks, the car unlocks, and it must be hotwired before it starts. The lock stays when the driver gets out, and its driver can also lock and unlock it from the seat (L / D-pad left). Errors if the entity is not a car or no longer exists.

methods.name: Lock
methods.doc: Lock the car. A locked car opens only for the last player who drove it: anyone else's vehicle key rattles the door, and holding the key breaks in -- the window on that side breaks, the car unlocks, and it must be hotwired before it starts. The lock stays when the driver gets out, and its driver can also lock and unlock it from the seat (L / D-pad left). Returns false when the entity is not a car.

methods.name: Refuel
methods.doc: Put amount of fuel in the tank (never above MaxFuel), or fill it when you leave amount out. Returns the fuel in the tank now. Example: Vehicles:Refuel(car, 20)

methods.name: Repair
methods.doc: Give the car amount of health back (never above MaxHealth), or all of it when you leave amount out. Returns the health it has now. A destroyed car drives again once it has any health.

methods.name: Seat
methods.doc: Put the player in the driver's seat, through the same checks as walking up and pressing the prompt: the player must be on foot, alive, near the car with a clear line to the seat, and the seat must be empty. Returns false when any of that refuses.

methods.name: SetBoost
methods.doc: Set the boost left, clamped to 0..MaxBoost.

methods.name: SetBoostDrain
methods.doc: Set how much boost is used each second while the driver boosts, from 0 up.

methods.name: SetBoostEnabled
methods.doc: Give the car a boost (true) or take it away (false). Off for every car until you turn it on. With boost on, its driver holds Shift (B on a gamepad) to push the car forward harder. Boost drains at BoostDrain a second while it pushes and comes back at BoostRegen a second when it does not. It starts full (MaxBoost, 100 unless you change it). A destroyed car or one with no fuel cannot boost.

methods.name: SetBoostRegen
methods.doc: Set how much boost comes back each second, from 0 up. 0 means a used boost never comes back by itself.

methods.name: SetBoostStrength
methods.doc: Set how hard the boost pushes, from 0 (nothing) to 1 (the hardest it can).

methods.name: SetFuel
methods.doc: Set the fuel, clamped to 0..MaxFuel. Fires Vehicles.FuelChanged, and Vehicles.FuelEmpty if it reaches 0.

methods.name: SetFuelConsumption
methods.doc: Set how much fuel the car burns each second while it is driven and moving, from 0 up. 0 means it never runs dry.

methods.name: SetFuelEnabled
methods.doc: Give the car a fuel tank (true) or take it away (false). Off for every car until you turn it on. With fuel on, the car burns FuelConsumption units a second while someone drives it and it is moving, and with none left it cannot accelerate (it rolls to a stop). It starts full (MaxFuel, 100 unless you change it).

methods.name: SetHealth
methods.doc: Set the car's health, clamped to 0..MaxHealth. Lowering it counts as damage (Vehicles.Damaged fires, and Vehicles.Destroyed if it reaches 0).

methods.name: SetHealthEnabled
methods.doc: Give the car health (true) or take it away again (false). It is off for every car until you turn it on, so a car you never touch crashes as it always did. With health on, crashes wear the car down (a hard enough crash wrecks it in one hit), and at 0 health the car is destroyed: it cannot accelerate until you Repair it. It starts full (MaxHealth, 100 unless you change it).

methods.name: SetLivery
methods.doc: Put one of the car's liveries on it: index counts from 0 in the liveries its vehicle was published with, and -1 takes the livery off. Every player sees the change. Returns false when the entity is not a car or the car has no livery at that index (the built-in cars have none).

methods.name: SetMaxBoost
methods.doc: Set the most boost the car can store, from 1 to 1,000,000.

methods.name: SetMaxFuel
methods.doc: Set the tank's size, from 1 to 1,000,000. Lowering it below the fuel lowers the fuel too; raising it does not fill the tank.

methods.name: SetMaxHealth
methods.doc: Set the most health the car can have, from 1 to 1,000,000. Lowering it below the car's health lowers the health too; raising it does not heal.

methods.name: SetPaintColor
methods.doc: Paint the car: color is "#RRGGBB", the same format as Backpack:SetWeaponColor. Returns false when the entity is not a car.

methods.name: Spawn
methods.doc: Spawn a car at position and return it as an Entity. item is the library item id of a vehicle this place stores: the string Storage:Get returns for one of the place's storage names. Any other value errors -- an asset id, an object path, a built-in car's name, an item the place does not store, or a weapon. The car is a real replicated vehicle: every player sees it, walks up to it and can drive it. Read its Position, tag it, or Destroy it like any entity. The server builds cars one per frame, so the Entity comes back at once but the car is not ready to use: connect to Vehicles.Ready, which fires with the car when it is built, before you Seat, paint or Lock it or touch its health, fuel or boost (those error until then).

methods.name: Unlock
methods.doc: Unlock the car, so anyone can open it again. A locked car opens only for the last player who drove it: anyone else's vehicle key rattles the door, and holding the key breaks in -- the window on that side breaks, the car unlocks, and it must be hotwired before it starts. The lock stays when the driver gets out, and its driver can also lock and unlock it from the seat (L / D-pad left). Returns false when the entity is not a car.

signals.name: BoostStarted
signals.doc: The car's driver started boosting.

signals.name: BoostStopped
signals.doc: The car's driver stopped boosting: let go of the key, ran out of boost, or the car lost its fuel or health.

signals.name: Damaged
signals.doc: The car lost health: a crash, Damage, or SetHealth to a lower number. amount is how much it lost and health what it has left. Only fires for a car you spawned with Vehicles:Spawn, once health is on.

signals.name: Destroyed
signals.doc: The car's health ran out. It cannot accelerate until it is repaired (Repair), so this is the moment to eject the driver, blow it up or remove it.

signals.name: FuelChanged
signals.doc: The car's fuel changed: it burns in steps of about a hundredth of MaxFuel, not every frame, or a script set or filled it. Arguments are the car, the old fuel, then the new.

signals.name: FuelEmpty
signals.doc: The car ran out of fuel and cannot accelerate until it is refuelled (Refuel).

signals.name: Ready
signals.doc: The car Vehicles:Spawn returned has been built and can be used: Seat, Lock, paint, livery, health, fuel and boost all work from here. The server builds spawned cars one per frame, so this fires a frame or more after Spawn (a burst of spawns takes that many frames). It fires once per spawn, also when the car was built at once. Connect before you Spawn or in the same script step; it only fires for a car you spawned with Vehicles:Spawn.

classes.name: Voice
classes.doc: Control who hears whom on voice chat, and see who is speaking.

methods.name: CanHear
methods.doc: Whether your rules let the listener hear the speaker. It does not know the players' own mutes and blocks, so a true here can still be silent for that listener.

methods.name: IsMuted
methods.doc: Whether you have muted this player for everyone with Voice:SetMuted. It says nothing about players' own mutes, and it is false while you have only muted them for some listeners.

methods.name: IsSpeaking
methods.doc: Whether the player is talking on voice chat right now. Each player's game tells the server whether they are talking (a yes or no, never audio), so it can lag by a fraction of a second, and a modified game could lie: use it for indicators and game play, not for anything that must be secure. A muted player still counts as speaking. On a client it covers the players this player can hear, themselves included. Example: if Voice:IsSpeaking(p) then ShowMicIcon(p) end

methods.name: MuteFor
methods.doc: Stop (true) or allow (false) one listener hearing one speaker; everyone else still hears the speaker. Use it for rules that depend on who is listening. Returns false when either player is not verified yet, or you already hold 4096 of these pairs. Lasts until either player leaves, or Voice:Reset. Example: for _, other in Players:GetPlayers() do Voice:MuteFor(other, dead, true) end -- the living cannot hear a dead player, who still hears them.

methods.name: Reset
methods.doc: Clear voice rules: every one that names player (muted, muted for someone, heard by an audience, or in one), or every rule on the server when you leave player out.

methods.name: SetAudience
methods.doc: Make a speaker heard only by the players in listeners (and by themselves); leave listeners out, or pass nil, to let everyone hear them again. This is team voice: set each player's audience to their team. At most 128 listeners. Returns false when the speaker is not verified yet or the list is too long. Lasts until the speaker leaves, or Voice:Reset. Mutes still apply on top. Example: Voice:SetAudience(p, Teams:GetPlayers(p.Team)) -- p's team hears p; call it again when teams change.

methods.name: SetMuted
methods.doc: Mute (true) or unmute (false) a player's voice for everyone: nobody hears them until you unmute them, though they can still talk. Use it for players who are dead, jailed or out of the round. Returns false when the player is not verified yet (moments after joining). The mute lasts until the player leaves. It only ever makes them quieter: a player who has muted or blocked someone themselves keeps them muted whatever you do. Voice goes straight between players' games, not through the server, so the server cannot hear or record it, and each listener's game applies the mute. A player running a modified game could ignore it, so use it to run a game, never to protect a secret. Example: Players:OnPlayer(function(p) Voice:SetMuted(p, true) end) -- everyone starts muted until a round begins, then Voice:SetMuted(p, false) for the players in it.

signals.name: SpeakingStarted
signals.doc: A player started talking on voice chat. Fires on the server (from the player's own report) and on clients (for players they can hear). Players with voice switched off never fire it.  Example: Voice.SpeakingStarted:Connect(function(p) print(p.Name .. " is talking") end)

signals.name: SpeakingStopped
signals.doc: A player stopped talking on voice chat. Fires wherever SpeakingStarted does.

methods.name: FindByTag
methods.doc: Every entity with this actor tag.

methods.name: FindFirst
methods.doc: The first entity whose name (actor label) matches, or nil.

methods.doc: Every entity and player character touching a box of this size (its full width, depth and height, at most 100 m on any side, kept square to the world's axes) centred on center, nearest first. Takes the same params as World:GetEntitiesInRadius.

methods.name: GetEntitiesInRadius

params.name: params
params.type: {Include: {Entity | Player}?, Exclude: {Entity | Player}?, Tag: string?, IgnorePlayers: boolean?, MaxResults: number?, Layers: {string}?, ExcludeLayers: {string}?}

methods.doc: Every entity and player character touching a ball of this radius (at most 50 m) around center, nearest first. Overlap-only entities (triggers) count; entities with no collision never do. A character is listed as its Entity; Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter tells whose it is. params: Include, Exclude, Tag, IgnorePlayers, Layers, ExcludeLayers (collision layers, server scripts only), and MaxResults (256 at most, and by default). Runs on this machine only; a script may make 256 spatial queries a frame.

methods.name: OnTagged
methods.doc: Call handler for every entity that has the tag now, and for each one that gets it later.

methods.name: OnUntagged
methods.doc: Call handler when an entity loses the tag.

methods.name: Raycast

params.name: params
params.type: {MaxDistance: number?, Include: {Entity | Player}?, Exclude: {Entity | Player}?, Tag: string?, IgnorePlayers: boolean?, Layers: {string}?, ExcludeLayers: {string}?}

methods.returns: {Entity: Entity, Player: Player?, Position: Vector3, Normal: Vector3, Distance: number}?
methods.doc: Cast a ray from origin along direction and return the first thing it hits: a table of Entity, Player, Position, Normal and Distance, or nil. Player is set when the hit is a player's character. The ray is as long as direction, or params.MaxDistance when given, and at most 1 km. It passes through overlap-only entities (triggers) and never hits entities with no collision. params: MaxDistance, Include (only these entities or players count), Exclude, Tag (only entities with this tag count), IgnorePlayers, Layers (only entities on these collision layers count; server scripts only) and ExcludeLayers (look through entities on these layers). Runs on this machine only; a script may make 256 spatial queries a frame.

methods.doc: Sweep a ball of this radius (at most 50 m) from origin along direction and return the first thing it touches, in the same table as World:Raycast, or nil. Distance is how far the ball's centre travelled. Takes the same params as World:Raycast.
